examples.en: These days, eating habits in Korea have become very westernized.

examples.ko: 도시가 빠르게 서구화하면서 전통 가게가 줄었어요.
examples.en: As the city westernized quickly, traditional shops decreased.

examples.ko: 할머니는 집 분위기가 너무 서구화하는 게 싫다고 하세요.
examples.en: Grandma says she doesn't like the home atmosphere becoming too westernized.

examples.ko: 옷차림만 서구화한 게 아니라 생각도 달라졌어요.
examples.en: It's not only the clothing that became westernized; the way of thinking changed too.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 한때 빨리 서구화하려고 애썼어요.
examples.en: That country once worked hard to westernize quickly.

examples.ko: 한옥을 서구화해서 카페로 꾸민 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many places where a hanok was westernized and made into a cafe.

explain: 생활 방식, 문화, 식습관, 제도처럼 바뀌는 것이 주어로 오면 '저절로 서양식이 되다'라는 느낌이고, '~을 서구화하다'라고 하면 누군가 바꾼다는 뜻이 돼요. 일상 대화에서는 '서양식으로 바뀌다'처럼 쉽게 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: When the thing that changes (lifestyle, culture, eating habits, systems) is the subject, it feels like it became Western on its own. With '~을 서구화하다', someone is making the change. In daily talk people often say it more simply, like '서양식으로 바뀌다'.

en: feel hurt and sorrowful; feel wronged

examples.ko: 동생이 혼자 집에 남게 되자 서러워했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling felt sad and hurt when left alone at home.

examples.ko: 그렇게 서러워하지 말고 저한테 이야기해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't feel so hurt; tell me about it.

examples.ko: 엄마는 아이가 서러워하는 모습을 보고 꼭 안아 주었어요.
examples.en: Mom saw the child feeling sad and hugged him tightly.

examples.ko: 억울하게 혼난 뒤 그는 한참 서러워했어요.
examples.en: After being scolded unfairly, he felt hurt for a long time.

examples.ko: 친구들이 동생만 빼고 놀러 가서 동생이 많이 서러워했어요.
examples.en: My friends went out without my younger sibling, so my sibling felt really hurt.

examples.ko: 나이가 들수록 작은 일에도 서러워하시는 분이 많아요.
examples.en: As people get older, many feel hurt even over small things.

explain: '서럽다'는 내 감정을 말할 때 쓰고('저 지금 서러워요'), '서러워하다'는 다른 사람이 그런 감정을 느끼는 모습을 말할 때 많이 써요. 외롭고 억울해서 속상한 마음이 섞여 있어요.
explain_en: '서럽다' is for your own feeling ('저 지금 서러워요'), while '서러워하다' is mostly used for describing someone else showing that feeling. It carries a mix of loneliness, unfairness and hurt.

examples.en: Please put the contract in the filing cabinet.

examples.ko: 필요한 서류는 책상 옆 서류함에 있어요.
examples.en: The documents you need are in the filing cabinet next to the desk.

examples.ko: 서류함이 꽉 차서 새 서류를 둘 곳이 없어요.
examples.en: The filing cabinet is full, so there's no place for new documents.

examples.ko: 사무실에 새 서류함을 하나 더 사야겠어요.
examples.en: I think we need to buy one more filing cabinet for the office.
I don't know where I put the key to the filing cabinet.

examples.ko: 받은 서류는 종류별로 서류함 안에 정리해요.
examples.en: I sort the documents I receive by type inside the file box.

explain: 종이 서류를 넣어 두는 서랍이나 상자를 말해요. 사무실에서 많이 쓰는 말이고, 앱이나 메일에서 파일을 모아 두는 곳은 '보관함' 같은 말을 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a drawer or box where paper documents are kept, and is a common office word. For places that store files in apps or email, people often use words like '보관함' (storage folder).

examples.en: It felt awkward at first with a friend I hadn't seen in a long time.
Since we fought, things have been awkward between me and my sibling.
I made a joke to break the awkward atmosphere.

examples.ko: 처음 만난 사람들이라 서먹서먹해서 말이 없었어요.
examples.en: We had just met, so it was awkward and nobody said much.

examples.ko: 이사 간 동네가 아직 서먹서먹하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: The neighborhood I moved to still feels unfamiliar.
We used to be awkward with each other, but now we keep in touch often.

explain: '어색하다'가 상황이나 행동 전체에 쓰인다면, '서먹서먹하다'는 사람 사이가 아직 친하지 않거나 멀어져서 불편한 느낌에 잘 어울려요. '서먹하다'로 줄여서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: '어색하다' can describe any awkward situation or behavior, but '서먹서먹하다' fits best when people aren't close yet or have drifted apart and feel uncomfortable. It is also shortened to '서먹하다'.

examples.en: We need housing policies for ordinary working people.

examples.ko: 이 시장은 서민층 손님이 많이 찾아요.
examples.en: Many ordinary customers visit this market.
When prices rise, ordinary people have the hardest time.
A drama about the lives of ordinary people is popular.
The government decided to give support money to ordinary households.

examples.ko: 그 동네는 서민층이 모여 사는 곳이에요.
examples.en: That neighborhood is where ordinary working people live.

explain: '서민'만 써도 같은 뜻이고, '서민층'은 사회를 계층으로 나눠 말할 때 써요. 반대는 '부유층'이고, 뉴스나 정책 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '서민' alone means the same thing, and '서민층' is used when talking about society in terms of social layers. The opposite is '부유층' (wealthy class), and it often appears in news and policy talk.

examples.en: There are many mountains in the northwest of this country.
It will snow in the northwestern region today.

examples.ko: 서북부 지역은 아침에 안개가 자주 껴요.
examples.en: The northwest area often has fog in the morning.
Our school is in the northwest part of the city.
Where do I take the bus going to the northwest?
Try finding the northwest part on the map.

explain: 어떤 지역의 서북쪽 부분을 말하고, '북서쪽'이라고도 해요. 날씨 예보나 지리 설명에서 지역 이름과 함께 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the northwest part of an area, and people also say '북서쪽'. It is often used with place names in weather forecasts and geography explanations.

examples.en: This singer is famous for lyrical song lyrics.

examples.ko: 영화의 서정적인 장면이 오래 기억에 남아요.
examples.en: The lyrical scenes of the movie stay in my memory for a long time.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 서정적인 음악이 듣고 싶어요.
examples.en: On rainy days, I want to listen to lyrical music.
That poet sings of nature in a lyrical way.
It's a cafe with a lyrical mood, so I go often.
The scenery was so lyrical that I took lots of photos.

explain: 감정이 부드럽고 아름답게 느껴지는 노래, 시, 풍경, 분위기에 써요. 실제로는 '서정적인', '서정적으로', '서정적이다'처럼 붙여서 쓰고, 이야기가 중심인 '서사적'과 대비되기도 해요.
explain_en: It describes songs, poems, scenery or moods that feel soft, emotional and beautiful. In practice it is used as '서정적인', '서정적으로' or '서정적이다', and it is sometimes contrasted with '서사적' (narrative).

examples.en: I put the meat on the grill and cook it.

examples.ko: 생선을 구울 때는 석쇠에 기름을 바르세요.
examples.en: When grilling fish, put oil on the grill.
The grill was too old, so I bought a new one.

examples.ko: 석쇠 자국이 선명한 구이가 맛있어 보여요.
examples.en: The grilled food with clear grill marks looks delicious.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 숯불 위 석쇠에서 오징어를 구우셨어요.
examples.en: Grandpa grilled squid on a grill over charcoal.

examples.ko: 캠핑 갈 때 석쇠를 꼭 챙겨 가요.
examples.en: I always bring a grill when I go camping.

explain: 불 위에 올려 음식을 직접 굽는 철망이에요. 석쇠에 구운 요리는 '석쇠구이'라고도 하고, 평평한 '불판'과는 모양이 달라요.
explain_en: It is a wire grate placed over a fire to cook food directly. Food cooked on it is also called '석쇠구이', and it differs in shape from a flat '불판' (grill plate).

examples.en: I eat both lunch and dinner at school.

examples.ko: 석식은 보통 저녁 여섯 시에 시작해요.
examples.en: Dinner usually starts at six in the evening.
What's on the dinner menu today?
We eat dinner before the evening study session.

examples.ko: 석식 신청을 안 해서 밖에서 사 먹었어요.
examples.en: I didn't sign up for dinner, so I bought some outside.

examples.ko: 급식실에서 석식을 신청한 학생만 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only students who signed up for dinner can eat in the cafeteria.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '저녁'이라고 하고, '석식'은 학교, 기숙사, 구내식당의 식단표에서 많이 봐요. '조식(아침), 중식(점심), 석식(저녁)'을 묶어서 기억하면 쉬워요.
explain_en: In daily talk people just say '저녁', while '석식' appears mostly on school, dorm and cafeteria menus. It is easy to remember together with '조식' (breakfast) and '중식' (lunch).

examples.en: Red evening light spread over the sea.
The sky tinted by the evening light is really pretty.
The evening sunlight comes warmly through the window.
The evening light slowly disappeared beyond the mountain.
The building looks golden in the evening light.
We walked slowly in the evening sunlight.

explain: 해가 질 때의 빛을 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '노을'이나 '노을빛'을 더 가볍게 쓰고, '석양빛'은 글이나 묘사에서 조금 더 분위기 있게 들려요.
explain_en: It means the light of the setting sun. In casual talk people use '노을' or '노을빛' more lightly, while '석양빛' sounds a bit more descriptive and literary.

examples.en: At the countryside house, we turn on the oil heater in winter.
We roasted and ate sweet potatoes next to the oil heater.

examples.ko: 석유난로를 켜 놓고 잘 때는 환기해야 해요.
examples.en: When you leave an oil heater on and sleep, you need to ventilate.
Please put oil into the oil heater.
There is an oil heater in the room at Grandma's house.
An electric heater is more convenient than an oil heater.

explain: 석유난로에 넣는 기름은 보통 '등유'라고 해요. 불을 쓰는 난로라서 환기와 안전에 꼭 주의해야 해요.
explain_en: The fuel put into an oil heater is usually called '등유' (kerosene). Because it uses a flame, you must be careful about ventilation and safety.

examples.en: In Korea, you have the right to vote from age 18.

examples.ko: 선거권이 없는 사람은 투표할 수 없어요.
examples.en: People without the right to vote cannot vote.

examples.ko: 법에 따라 일정한 나이가 되면 선거권이 주어져요.
examples.en: By law, you are given the right to vote once you reach a certain age.
A long time ago, women did not have the right to vote.

examples.ko: 처음 선거권을 얻은 날 투표소에 갔어요.
examples.en: On the day I first got the right to vote, I went to the polling station.

examples.ko: 선거권을 가진 사람은 꼭 투표하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's good for people with the right to vote to be sure to vote.

explain: 투표할 수 있는 권리예요. 짝이 되는 말은 선거에 나갈 수 있는 권리인 '피선거권'이고, '선거권이 있다/없다/주어지다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the right to cast a vote. Its counterpart is '피선거권', the right to run in an election, and it is used as '선거권이 있다/없다/주어지다'.

examples.en: I hope the economy changes into a virtuous-cycle structure.

examples.ko: 운동하면 잠이 잘 오고, 잠을 잘 자면 또 운동하고 싶은 선순환이 생겨요.
examples.en: Exercise helps you sleep well, and sleeping well makes you want to exercise again, creating a virtuous circle.

examples.ko: 소비가 늘면 생산도 늘어서 선순환이 이어져요.
examples.en: When spending grows, production also grows, and a virtuous circle continues.
Try creating a virtuous circle of praise and effort.
Good habits can also lead to a virtuous circle.

examples.ko: 이 정책은 지역 경제의 선순환을 목표로 해요.
examples.en: This policy aims at a virtuous circle in the local economy.

explain: 좋은 결과가 다시 좋은 원인이 되어 계속 좋아지는 흐름이에요. 반대말은 '악순환'이고, '선순환 구조', '선순환이 되다/이어지다'처럼 경제 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a flow in which a good result becomes the cause of further good results. The opposite is '악순환' (vicious circle), and it appears often in economic news as '선순환 구조' or '선순환이 되다/이어지다'.

examples.ko: 첫인상 때문에 선입관을 갖지 않으려고 해요.
examples.en: I try not to form preconceptions because of first impressions.
Try eating it once without any preconceptions.
My preconception about that person was broken.

examples.ko: 외모만 보고 선입관을 가지면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't form preconceptions just by looking at appearance.
I missed a good chance because of my preconception.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 선입관과 달리 정말 재미있었어요.
examples.en: Unlike what I assumed, that movie was really fun.

explain: '편견'은 한쪽으로 치우친 나쁜 생각에 가깝고, '선입관'은 직접 겪기 전에 미리 가진 생각이라 좋은 쪽일 수도 있어요. '선입견'이라고도 하고, '선입관을 갖다/버리다/깨다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '편견' leans toward a biased, negative view, while '선입관' is an idea formed before experiencing something, which can even be positive. It is also said '선입견', and used as '선입관을 갖다/버리다/깨다'.

examples.ko: 나라의 교육 제도를 선진화해야 한다는 목소리가 커요.
examples.en: There are growing calls to modernize the country's education system.
They increased research funding to advance the industry.
There were many difficulties in the process of advancement.
The government promised to advance the medical system.

examples.ko: 교통의 선진화가 도시를 더 편하게 만들어요.
examples.en: Advancing transportation makes the city more convenient.
It takes a long time for advancement to be achieved.

explain: 제도, 산업, 기술, 시스템이 선진국 수준으로 발전하는 것을 말해서 뉴스나 정책 이야기에 많이 나와요. 사람에게는 쓰지 않고, 일상에서는 '발전하다'처럼 더 쉬운 말을 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It means systems, industries and technology reaching the level of developed countries, so it shows up in news and policy talk. It is not used for people, and in daily speech simpler words like '발전하다' are often used.

examples.en: The company decided to modernize its way of working.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 교통 시스템을 선진화해서 편해졌어요.
examples.en: This city advanced its transport system and became more convenient.

examples.ko: 병원 시설을 선진화하려면 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Modernizing hospital facilities costs a lot of money.
The government announced that it will modernize agriculture.
Thanks to modernizing the system, the procedures became simpler.
Opposing opinions also came up during the modernization process.

explain: 제도, 시설, 산업처럼 일이나 체계를 더 발전된 수준으로 만들 때 써요. 사람에게는 쓰지 않고, 더 쉬운 말로는 '발전시키다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is used for making things like systems, facilities and industries more advanced. It is not used for people, and a simpler alternative is '발전시키다'.

examples.ko: 이 수업은 선택적으로 들을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can take this class optionally.
Participation is optional, so it's fine if you don't come.

examples.ko: 이 항목은 선택적이라서 비워 두셔도 돼요.
examples.en: This item is optional, so you may leave it blank.
People sometimes remember things selectively.
This option is not required but optional.

examples.ko: 선택적 기능은 설정에서 켤 수 있어요.
examples.en: Optional features can be turned on in the settings.

explain: 반대는 '필수적'이에요. 사전에는 관형사로 나오지만 실제로는 '선택적으로', '선택적이다', '선택적 참여'처럼 많이 붙여 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '필수적' (required). Dictionaries list it as a determiner, but in practice it is used as '선택적으로', '선택적이다' or '선택적 참여'.

examples.en: The rice was undercooked, so I had to cook it again.

examples.ko: 고기가 설익으면 배탈이 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the meat is undercooked, you may get a stomachache.
Undercooked potatoes are hard and difficult to eat.
The fruit is still not ripe, so it doesn't taste good.

examples.ko: 불을 너무 일찍 꺼서 면이 설익었어요.
examples.en: I turned off the heat too early, so the noodles are undercooked.

examples.ko: 설익은 밥에는 물을 조금 넣고 다시 익히세요.
examples.en: Add a little water to undercooked rice and cook it again.

explain: '덜 익다'와 비슷하지만 한 단어로 쓰는 말이고, 밥, 고기, 과일에 모두 쓸 수 있어요. 활용은 '설익어요, 설익은, 설익었어요'이고, 비슷한 '덜 익다'는 띄어 써요.

phrases.en: If you decide with an immature idea, you'll regret it later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 아니라 생각이나 주장이 충분히 다듬어지지 않았다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not for food but for an idea or claim that isn't well thought out yet.

explain_en: It is similar to '덜 익다' but is a single word, and works for rice, meat and fruit. It conjugates as '설익어요, 설익은, 설익었어요', while '덜 익다' is written with a space.

examples.en: Mosquitoes keep buzzing and it's so annoying.

examples.ko: 자꾸 오는 영업 전화가 성가셔서 받지 않아요.
examples.en: Sales calls keep coming and they're bothersome, so I don't answer.

examples.ko: 서류 절차가 복잡해서 성가신 일이 많아요.
examples.en: The paperwork is complicated, so there are many tiresome things.
My younger sibling kept following me, and it felt bothersome.
If it's not too much trouble, could you help me with this?

examples.ko: 하루에도 몇 번씩 오는 광고 문자가 성가셨어요.
examples.en: The ad messages that came several times a day were annoying.

explain: '귀찮다'와 비슷하지만 '성가시다'는 자꾸 신경 쓰이고 방해가 되는 느낌이 강해요. 부탁할 때 '성가시게 해서 죄송해요'처럼 정중하게 쓰기도 하고, 활용은 '성가셔요, 성가신'이에요.
explain_en: It is close to '귀찮다', but '성가시다' stresses the feeling of something repeatedly bothering or interrupting you. It is also used politely when asking favors, as in '성가시게 해서 죄송해요', and conjugates as '성가셔요, 성가신'.

examples.en: I tried sea urchin seaweed soup in Jeju.

examples.ko: 성게는 가시가 많아서 조심해서 만져야 해요.
examples.en: Sea urchins have many spines, so you must touch them carefully.
I saw a person catching sea urchins at the beach.
This sea urchin roe is nutty and sweet, so it's delicious.
A sea urchin is stuck between the rocks.
This restaurant is famous for its sea urchin bibimbap.

explain: 먹는 부분은 '성게알'이라고 불러서 메뉴에는 '성게알'이라고 적힌 경우도 많아요. 가시가 있는 바다 동물이라 바닷가에서 만지면 위험할 수 있어요.
explain_en: The edible part is called '성게알' (sea urchin roe), so menus often use that word. It is a spiny sea animal, so touching one at the beach can be dangerous.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 성깔이 있어서 화나면 무서워요.
examples.en: That person has a temper, so he's scary when angry.

examples.ko: 성깔 있는 고양이라서 아무나 만지면 안 돼요.
examples.en: It's a cat with a temper, so not just anyone should touch it.
My father is a bit hot-tempered.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 성깔을 못 참고 자주 싸웠어요.
examples.en: When I was young, I couldn't hold my temper and often fought.
Don't throw a fit; let's talk calmly.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 성깔이 대단해서 선생님도 힘들어하세요.
examples.en: That child has a fierce temper, so even the teacher finds it hard.

explain: 화를 잘 내는 거친 성질을 말하고 '성깔이 있다, 성깔이 사납다, 성깔을 부리다'처럼 써요. 조금 구어적이고 부정적인 느낌이라서 윗사람에게는 '성격'이나 '성품'이 더 안전해요.
explain_en: It refers to a rough, easily angered nature, used as '성깔이 있다, 성깔이 사납다, 성깔을 부리다'. It is somewhat colloquial and negative, so '성격' or '성품' is safer when speaking about elders.

examples.en: I made a small house model with matchsticks.
I lit the candle with a single matchstick.
The matchstick got wet, so it won't light.
I picked up the matchstick that fell on the floor.
It is dangerous to give matchsticks to a child.
He is thin as a matchstick, so I'm worried.

explain: '성냥'은 전체를 말하고, '성냥개비'는 막대 하나를 가리킬 때 잘 어울려요. 요즘은 라이터를 더 많이 쓰지만, 만들기나 옛날이야기에서 아직 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '성냥' refers to matches in general, while '성냥개비' fits best when pointing to a single stick. Lighters are more common today, but matchsticks still come up in crafts and old stories.

examples.ko: 친구가 선생님 성대모사를 해서 다 웃었어요.
examples.en: My friend did an impression of the teacher and everyone laughed.
I envy people who are good at impersonating voices.

examples.ko: 그 가수 성대모사 좀 해 보세요.
examples.en: Do an impression of that singer for us.
My child keeps imitating the cartoon character's voice.
I laughed for a long time watching a voice impression video.
The voice is so similar that the impression sounds real.

explain: 다른 사람이나 동물의 목소리를 똑같이 흉내 내는 것에 써요. '성대모사(를) 하다'라고 하고, '흉내 내다'는 목소리뿐 아니라 동작까지 포함할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is for copying another person's or animal's voice closely, used as '성대모사(를) 하다'. '흉내 내다' can cover not just voice but also actions.

examples.ko: 추석 아침에는 차례를 지내고 곧바로 성묘해요.
examples.en: On Chuseok morning, we hold the ancestral rite and go straight to visit the graves.

examples.ko: 성묘를 마친 뒤 가족들과 근처 식당에서 점심을 먹었어요.
examples.en: After finishing the grave visit, we ate lunch with family at a nearby restaurant.

examples.ko: 추석 다음 날 여유 있게 성묘했어요.
examples.en: The day after Chuseok, we visited the grave at a relaxed pace.
I went down to my hometown to visit Grandpa's grave.

examples.ko: 성묘할 때 산소 주변의 풀을 정리해요.
examples.en: When visiting the grave, we tidy up the grass around it.

examples.ko: 올해는 비가 와서 성묘를 못 갔어요.
examples.en: It rained this year, so we couldn't go to the grave.

explain: 주로 설, 추석, 한식 같은 때에 조상의 산소에 가는 일에 써요. '성묘하다'보다 '성묘(를) 가다/다녀오다'도 자주 쓰고, 산소는 '묘'보다 '산소'가 더 부드러운 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used for visiting ancestors' graves, mainly around Seol, Chuseok and Hansik. People often say '성묘(를) 가다/다녀오다' as well as '성묘하다', and '산소' is a gentler word than '묘' for a grave.

examples.ko: 사람의 성숙도는 나이와 꼭 같지 않아요.
examples.en: A person's maturity is not always the same as their age.
Each child's emotional maturity is different.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 작가의 성숙도를 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This novel shows the author's maturity.
I'm often surprised by my friend's maturity.
The maturity of civic awareness changes society.

examples.ko: 성숙도가 높은 사람은 감정을 잘 조절해요.
examples.en: People with high maturity control their emotions well.

explain: 얼마나 성숙했는지 그 정도를 말하고, '성숙도가 높다/낮다'처럼 써요. 사람뿐 아니라 사회, 작품에도 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '어른스럽다'가 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It expresses the degree of how mature something is, used as '성숙도가 높다/낮다'. It applies to people, societies and works, and in everyday talk '어른스럽다' is often more natural.

examples.en: Exports kept up their growth trend this year.
I saw news that the growth trend has weakened.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 몇 년째 빠른 성장세를 보여요.
examples.en: This company has shown fast growth for several years.
We must work so that the growth trend doesn't break.
The online shopping market has a clear growth trend.

examples.ko: 성장세에 힘입어 직원을 더 뽑기로 했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the growth trend, they decided to hire more staff.

explain: 경제나 회사, 시장이 커지는 흐름을 말하고 '성장세를 보이다/이어 가다', '성장세가 꺾이다'처럼 써요. 주로 뉴스와 경제 이야기에 나오고, 사람의 키가 크는 일에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It describes the flow of an economy, company or market growing, used as '성장세를 보이다/이어 가다' or '성장세가 꺾이다'. It mainly appears in news and economic talk, and is not used for a person's physical growth.
